events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The rider's complaint is that the Tiong Bahru Market stop caused an overcharged detour [F1]. The trip ran Clarke Quay → VivoCity, billed 7.83 km against an optimal 5.6 km, with one off-route segment 17:31–17:39 adding 1.39 km and the car stationary 4 minutes at the market location [F4][F2]. The metered total of $20.46 includes distance of $11.04 and platform fee $1.47, with no surge and no waiting charge [F7][F6].

The single off-route segment is excused by RD-3. Before the segment began the rider messaged at 17:28: "Can you stop by Tiong Bahru Market first? 5 min." and the driver replied "Ok" [F8][F9]. The rider therefore named the specific place and the driver accepted, and the car did stop there for 4 minutes [F2]. Under RD-3 (A7/A9) that segment is not a deviation, and the way to the named stop is part of the stop, so the segment is not split — the whole segment is exempt [F8][F9][F2][F4]. The driver's post-trip statement that one-way streets made the approach longer [F11] is his own account and, with no traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F14], does not exempt anything on its own; it is RD-3, not RD-4, that disposes of this segment. Because the record places the segment at the named stop, RD-5 does not govern it: the agreement is to the rider's named place, not to a driver-proposed route [F8][F4].

With the segment exempt, the refundable distance is the deviation under RD-1/RD-2 less the exempt km: (2.25 km − 2.25 km exempt) × $1.4100/km = $0.00 [F5][F4]. What remains is 0 km, i.e. within RD-1's 1 km tolerance, so no refund arises and the charge stands [F5][RD-1][RD-2]. Nothing here shows a prior upheld route dispute, so no account flag under RD-6 arises [F17].

The safety screen is clear: the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 escalation applies [F8][F9][F11]. The record settles every element: full GPS coverage with segments and stop location, timestamped messages, and a fare build-up, so the evidence is sufficient and no gap remains [F10][F2][F4][F7]. Both briefs ask for no_action; no claim of the losing side needs separate rejection beyond the rider's overcharge theory, which fails because the extra distance is the rider's own requested stop.
